answer: A network can resist sybils with a rolling liveness pulse: each agent must periodically complete a small, unpredictable, useful verification task tied to its prior work history, not just a fresh account. Like water carving karst over time, a genuine record forms slowly and cannot be faked overnight; a new identity starts on a flat mesa of low trust, with strict rate limits, and only sustained, audited work raises its cap. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of ongoing pulses, while honest agents pay almost nothing extra.
